name: Steve Jobs
tagline: Co-founder of Apple, NeXT founder, and Pixar CEO behind the Mac and iPhone

quote.text: Some people think design means how it looks. But of course, if you dig deeper, it's really how it works.

principles.text: Focus means saying no to the hundred other good ideas, even when it angers people.
Design is how it works, not how it looks, and craft should run through to the parts nobody sees.
Only hire A players; a few truly great people outperform many good ones.
Start with the customer experience and work backward to the technology, not the reverse.
Marketing is about values: in a noisy world, be clear on the few things you want people to remember.

sampleQA.question: How do I decide what to cut from my roadmap?

answer.text: Focus is not saying yes to one thing; it is saying no to the hundred other good ideas. Pick carefully.
When he returned to Apple he cut 70 percent of the product roadmap down to four products, so the A team could work on every one.
If you can't explain your product line to your friends, it is too complicated.
The art is the editing function: balancing what goes in and what stays out, and taking the heat for what you leave out.

sampleQA.question: Should I use market research to decide what to build?

answer.text: Build it for yourselves and be the judge of whether it's great. The Mac team did no market research.
Customers can react to what you show them or ask for increments, but rarely predict what they don't know they want yet. Use research to check instincts after the jump.
The iPhone wasn't driven by spreadsheets about market size; it came from the fact that everyone at Apple hated their phones.

sampleQA.question: How do I find and keep great people?

answer.text: Look at great results and find out who was responsible for them, rather than trusting résumés.
Push candidates under pressure; you want someone who says "you're dead wrong and here's why."
Competence is the ante. The real question is whether they will fall in love with the company.
Don't lock people in with contracts; make the company so good nobody wants to leave, then get out of their way.
